title.narrative: Output 1.5: National dissemination conference on report of rights of pretrial detainees organized

description.narrative: As previously reported, EHRC released the report on the national inquiry carried out in four regions, Amhara, Oromia, Somali regions, as well as on the previous Southern Nations and Nationalities and peoples on March 22, 2024. The Commission disseminated the report and initiated discussion on the findings and implementation of the recommendations on December 18, 2024, in Addis Ababa with stakeholders from federal and regional governments, representatives from the international community, and stakeholders from civil society organizations. EHRC had also organized a dissemination conference in December 2022 to share the findings and recommendations of the public hearing in SNNPR, and follow up on actions taken by the federal and regional authorities in Hawassa.

title.narrative: Increased coordination of the provision of legal aid by NGOs, university based law clinics, and other legal aid service providers

description.narrative: EHRC hosted a national conference on April 2324, 2025, in Addis Ababa to address challenges in the accessibility and quality of free legal aid services. The event convened key stakeholders from government institutions, civil society, academia, and legal advocacy groups to foster dialogue and collaboration on the provision of accessible and quality legal aid service. International partners, including UN agencies and human rights organizations, also participated, reinforcing the conferences broad support and impact.A multistakeholder committeecomprising federal and regional government institutions, civil society organizations, and legal aid providerswas formed following the national legal aid conference to develop a joint action plan. EHRC leads the initiative and international development partners have committed to providing technical support. This mechanism marks a significant step toward structured and collaborative legal aid service provision in Ethiopia.

title.narrative: Enhanced capacity to provide oversight, provide redress for victims of human rights violations of users of the criminal justice system, and to hold justice institutions to account

description.narrative: There are two indicators proposed, in the revised logframe, to enable us to measure the progress and achievement of the first outcome. To measure Outcome Indicator 1.1, we count the number of complaints of human rights violations EHRC receives using its electronic case management system. Accordingly, from September 2024 to April 2025, EHRC received a total of 921 complaints of human rights violations representing 1100 complainants from all its offices. Fifty four percent of the complaints are about civil and political rights. Out of these, EHRC received and investigated 116 complaints related to the right to liberty and security; 148 complaints related to the rights of arrested persons; and 14 complaints related to freedom from torture and cruel treatment. The electronic case management system EHRC uses for its complaint handling service classifies complaints in relation to the right to liberty and security under one category, while it classifies complaints related to freedom from torture and cruel treatment and rights of arrested persons separately. Disaggregated data on the right to liberty and right to security is thus not available. For this particular indicator, the number of complaints related to the abovementioned rights are added up to a total of 116 as they relate to persons deprived of their liberty. The target is not achieved because when the target was set, it was anticipated that EHRC will, at least, open branch offices in 23 regions where it does not have physical presence. However, not only it was not able to open additional branch offices due to financial constraints, because of the conflict in the North, its office in Mekelle was closed down for over two years, before it reopened in November 2024. In addition, due to the conflict in Amhara, EHRC was only able to conduct very few monitoring visits to police stations and prisons in the last two years, during which it also receives and handles complaints on the right to liberty and security.The institutions against which complaints are lodged against the most are the regional police commissions (close to 35% of the alleged perpetrators), followed by regional police commission (5% of the alleged perpetrators); Federal Prison Commission (5% of alleged perpetrators); and the Ethiopian Defense Forces (4% of the alleged perpetrators).From September 2024 to April 2025, 14% complaints were made by women, and close to 4% of the complainants are children (persons under 18 years of age); while 5% of the complainants are persons with disability. Out of these, 54% of the complaints concern violations of civil and political rights, including human rights violations of persons deprived of their liberty (unlawful detention, arbitrary arrest, not bringing them to the court of law, access to health care, denial of speedy trial, extrajudicial killing, disappearance, right to bail). The target is not achieved despite the fact that EHRC engaged with different nongovernmental organizations working with women and children and promoted its complaint mechanisms. There is need to further conduct an assessment in partnership with womenled and childled organizations to identify how to make EHRCs complaint mechanism more accessible to women and children.
